title: Ice Protection — Slat Piccolo Ducts — Installation of Bellows-Compensated Support Brackets
abstract: Completion of the slat piccolo duct supports to the bellows-compensated standard, replacing the sliding brackets that let the ducts walk outboard under repeated anti-ice thermal cycling.

sections.planning_reason: Leading edge surveys at heavy maintenance found piccolo ducts displaced from their nominal position by up to 14 mm, always outboard and always in the same direction. Bench testing reproduced the mechanism: the sliding bracket lets the duct grow under anti-ice heating and grips slightly on cool-down, so the duct ratchets over thousands of cycles. Two aircraft were found with a cracked bracket foot. No anti-ice performance loss has been reported, but the displacement eventually loads the duct end fitting in bending and the trend is one way.
sections.description: Each sliding bracket is replaced by a fixed foot with a short bellows section that absorbs the axial growth. The duct non-return valve is repositioned 25 mm inboard so that the bellows sits in a straight run, and the heat exchanger mounting is re-drilled to suit. A guard is fitted over the bellows to protect it during leading edge access work.
sections.accomplishment_summary: With the fixed leading edge already open and the slats at the maintenance position, record the existing duct position at each bracket before anything is disturbed. Disconnect the duct hose 203WX and support the duct run. Remove the sliding brackets and clean the rib faces. Install the fixed feet with rivets LN907384-1B and set the bellows section to the free length given in the accomplishment instructions. Reposition the non-return valve D3010128666060 25 mm inboard and re-drill the heat exchanger D3010120571398 mounting. Fit the bellows guard with screws AGS212130-5E. Do a duct pressure and leak check, then a wing anti-ice functional test. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00393. Aircraft from the production cut-in onward already carry the bellows arrangement. There is no pre-modification or post-modification condition, but the aircraft must not carry an open duct displacement finding when the work starts.
sections.material_note: Kit K3010-1037-01 covers one aircraft, both wings. Lead time is eighteen weeks. The bellows sections are supplied at their free length and must not be compressed in storage. Removed sliding brackets are not returnable.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled leading edge opening, or within 72 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

title: Ice Protection — Slat Piccolo Ducts — Installation of Bellows-Compensated Support Brackets

issue.reason: Reissued as an in-service instruction with the leading edge access, the drain provisions and the reinstatement checks that the line completion did not need.

abstract: Replacement of the sliding piccolo duct supports by a bellows-compensated arrangement, which stops the ducts walking outboard under repeated anti-ice thermal cycling and deletes the duct position check.

sections.planning_reason: Leading edge surveys at heavy maintenance found piccolo ducts displaced from their nominal position by up to 14 mm, always outboard and always in the same direction. Bench testing reproduced the mechanism: the sliding bracket lets the duct grow under anti-ice heating and grips slightly on cool-down, so the duct ratchets over thousands of cycles. Two aircraft were found with a cracked bracket foot. No anti-ice performance loss has been reported, but the displacement eventually loads the duct end fitting in bending and the trend is one way.
sections.description: Each sliding bracket is replaced by a fixed foot with a short bellows section that absorbs the axial growth. The duct non-return valve is repositioned 25 mm inboard so that the bellows sits in a straight run, and the heat exchanger mounting is re-drilled to suit. A guard is fitted over the bellows to protect it during leading edge access work. This revision does not change the bracket content. It adds what an aircraft in service needs and a wing on the line does not: opening and closing the fixed leading edge bay by bay, restoring the drainage provisions disturbed by the work, and proving the bay before it is closed.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Extend the slats to the maintenance position and install the ground lock; make the anti-ice system safe at the maintenance panel. Remove the fixed leading edge panels in zones 551, 553 and 512, one bay at a time, and support each panel clear of the slat track. Do the inspection task AMM-M-30-10-12-200-017-A and record the existing duct position at each bracket before anything is disturbed. Note the position of every drain path in the bay and mask the two rib drain holes at each bracket before any swarf is made; a blocked rib drain holds water against the lower skin and is the most common finding after this work. Disconnect the duct hose 203WX and support the duct run. Remove the sliding brackets and clean the rib faces. Install the fixed feet with rivets LN907384-1B and set the bellows section to the free length given in the accomplishment instructions. Reposition the non-return valve D3010128666060 25 mm inboard and re-drill the heat exchanger D3010120571398 mounting; collect the swarf at the drill and vacuum the bay before the masking is removed. Fit the bellows guard with screws AGS212130-5E. Restore the harness clamping to the position given on the leading edge wiring sheet, which moves with the bracket. Remove the masking, prove every rib drain clear with the drain probe and restore the sealant at each disturbed rib face. Do a duct pressure and leak check, then a wing anti-ice functional test. Close the leading edge bay by bay, do a slat retraction and extension check with the ground lock removed and confirm that no panel fastener is missing. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00393. Aircraft from the production cut-in onward already carry the bellows arrangement. There is no pre-modification or post-modification condition, but the aircraft must not carry an open duct displacement finding when the work starts.
sections.material_note: Kit K3010-1037-01 covers one aircraft, both wings. Lead time is eighteen weeks. The bellows sections are supplied at their free length and must not be compressed in storage. Removed sliding brackets are not returnable. The kit does not include the fixed leading edge panel fastener set or the rib face sealant, both of which are consumed by the in-service accomplishment and must be ordered separately; a panel fastener disturbed by this work is not to be reused.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled leading edge opening, or within 72 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: In-service access, drain provisions and reinstatement checks added
